framing_issues.text: County justice leaders and Commissioner Dana Barrett have objected to how the draft is being made.
framing_issues.issue: The 30-second version names only the critics' position. The supporters' stated case (P-004: earlier input with balanced north and south representation; Ellis, P-073 and P-079: open meetings, full Board votes) is left out of the summary most readers will see. Suggest adding: 'Supporters, including Commissioner Ellis, say it adds earlier input while the full Board still decides.'

framing_issues.text: They sent the Board a letter and said they would skip the commission's budget hearings.
framing_issues.issue: 'Skip' is informal and implies neglect. The sources say they declined live presentations (P-076, P-078: 'respectfully decline') and submitted written 2027 requests (P-080). That missing context makes them look less engaged than the sources describe.

framing_issues.text: A resolution to remove a 5% cap on department budget requests failed. (also line 99 heading 'failed and filed', line 109, line 117, line 160)
framing_issues.issue: The procedural term is misused. The record says the motion to approve failed on Oct 21 (P-024); the resolution stayed pending and was filed on Nov 4. Line 102 states it correctly, so the page is inconsistent.

framing_issues.text: Its sponsor, Commissioner Dana Barrett, voted yes, and Commissioner Ellis voted no.
framing_issues.issue: Only Ellis is named on the losing side. The result also turned on two members not voting (Chairman Pitts, and Commissioner Arrington, who had seconded the motion, P-025) and two absent (Thorne and Vice Chair Abdur-Rahman, P-033). Naming one voter singles him out.

framing_issues.text: The same agenda listed a discussion, led by the vice chair, ...
framing_issues.issue: 'Led by' is an inference from '(Abdur-Rahman)' on the agenda (P-038). Right after her motion to file, it suggests coordination the record does not show.
Missing context: the $50 million for the jail consent decree is budgeted under Non Agency (P-054), not in the sheriff's line, so readers may underestimate jail-related spending.

framing_issues.text: ...entered an agreement with the United States Department of Justice to fix conditions at the Fulton County Jail.
framing_issues.issue: This softens the county's own words, 'to address constitutional violations' (P-048).

framing_issues.text: So the reasons for the process are thinly documented here, though the process has stayed in place after each vote.
framing_issues.issue: An adjective that takes sides, plus a 'though' contrast, implying the majority keeps a process it cannot justify. The resolution's stated reasons (P-004, P-007) were mentioned just before. No matching caveat is given about how thin the critics' evidence is. The page also says twice (lines 105, 111) that the majority gave no reasons.

framing_issues.text: The vice chair, who also serves on the commission, had not answered Atlanta News First when it published.
framing_issues.issue: 'Had not answered' can read as evasive. The source says the outlet 'is still waiting to hear back' (P-073). A neutral version: 'Atlanta News First said it had not heard back from the vice chair.'

framing_issues.text: Ellis noted that the full Board will review and vote on the final budget, FOX 5 reported. (also line 150)
framing_issues.issue: Uneven verbs: Ellis 'noted' (a verb that presumes the statement is true), while critics 'said'. Here the statement is true (P-014), but using 'said' for everyone keeps parity.

framing_issues.text: Card 2 evidence label 'Supported, with limits' vs card 4 'Uncertain' (rules at line 115)
framing_issues.issue: The evidence labels are uneven between sides. By the page's own rule, a missing key document means 'Uncertain'. Card 2 (supporters) lacks the written 5% instruction yet is labeled 'Supported, with limits', a label the rules don't define. Card 4 (critics) is 'Uncertain'. Card 6's side, 'county justice leaders', fits neither group in the ordering rule.

framing_issues.text: Commissioner Dana Barrett's resolution sought "to ensure transparency" and ...
framing_issues.issue: Listed under 'Who disagrees' with 'The new process is open', but the resolution does not say the meetings are closed. It concerns which requests appear in the proposed budget, so the disagreement is overstated.

framing_issues.text: Whether needs are hidden can't be checked until the draft is out.
framing_issues.issue: 'Hidden' takes the critics' loaded word into the page's own analysis. Suggest: 'Whether the draft will show needs above 5% can't be checked until it is out.'

framing_issues.text: Solicitor-General Keith Gammage said, "Each year we are underfunded."
framing_issues.issue: Out of context: in its source (P-071, Atlanta News First) the remark is about his office's funding, not the 5% limit. Under 'Who says it' on the 5% card, it gives him a stated position on the cap that the passage does not show.

framing_issues.text: The Board filed the resolution that would have removed it, 4 to 1.
framing_issues.issue: Placed under 'Who disagrees', the filing vote assigns disagreement with the critics' claim to the four members who voted to file. The page itself says they gave no reasons (lines 105, 111), and filing may have had other motives.

framing_issues.text: Commissioner Ellis said there is no talk of an early vote, Atlanta News First reported.
framing_issues.issue: Under 'Who disagrees' on the wait-until-January card, a named official's statement that fits waiting may read as opposition.

framing_issues.text: In 2026, justice and safety got $507.5 million ... Last year's proposal said there was no money for program additions ...
framing_issues.issue: Selective use of a source. P-049's next sentence, 'additional resources will be needed for consent decree compliance', supports the justice offices and is left out. Also, a 48% share of spending shows scale, not that funding is adequate, so it is a weak 'challenge'.

framing_issues.text: The 2026 budget set aside $50,000,000 ... Last year's proposal said ...
framing_issues.issue: Missing context: the same passage (P-050) reports a '1% Reduction across all Agencies/Departments' ($10 million) in last year's budget. That across-the-board measure bears on the cap debate and on the GFOA quote about across-the-board cuts or caps (card 4).

framing_issues.text: Should departments' first requests be limited, or should the Board see every request in full?
framing_issues.issue: Uneven wording: one option is framed as a restriction ('limited') and the other as a benefit ('see every request in full'). Parallel wording: 'Should departments' requests be capped at a set percentage, or should every request be listed in full?'
